newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria needs economic reforms - Britain's Rifkind.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria needs economic reforms - Britain's Rifkind.

text.p: Fundamental economic reforms are urgently needed in Bulgaria, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Wednesday as it was announced he will make his first visit to the country next week.
The Foreign Office said Rifkind will be in Sofia on January 28 and 29 for talks with new President Petar Stoyanov and other senior officials.

Before that, he will pay a 1-1/2 day visit to Romania where he will meet President Emil Constantinescu to discuss the priorities of the new government and the enlargement of the European Union and North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
Stoyanov, who was officially sworn in on Wednesday, faces a major challenge as he takes over from outgoing president Zhelyu Zhelev.

Politicians in Bulgaria are deadlocked over the formation of a new cabinet, the country is on the verge of defaulting on its $10 billion foreign debt and there have been 15 days of protests by opposition parties demanding fresh elections.
"Bulgaria is in a difficult economic and political situation," Rifkind said. "Fundamental economic reform measures have been delayed too long and are now urgently needed."
"I want to make clear that the United Kingdom will do what it can to support this process," he added.
Rifkind's visit will be the first to Bulgaria by a British Foreign Secretary since his predecessor Douglas Hurd went there in 1993.
